0.0.n: Refers to the deeper part of the place being visited.

0.1.n: Marks 奥 as the location of the decoration.

0.2.n: Makes the location the topic, shifting attention further inside.

0.3.n: The adverb form of すごい strengthens 大きな.

0.4.n: This form goes directly before a noun, here 組紐の飾り.

0.5.n: Refers to traditional Japanese cords made by braiding threads.

0.6.n: Links 組紐 to 飾り, describing what kind of decoration it is.

0.7.n: A noun referring to the large braided ornament on display.

0.8.n: Adds this decoration to other things seen; the sentence leaves out the verb.

1.0.n: Describes the strong visual impact of the decoration.

1.1.n: Marks 迫力 as what was impressive.

1.2.n: すごかった is the past form of すごい; です makes the comment polite.

1.4.n: Describes how the speaker looks, rather than how often.

1.5.n: The plain form of 見る comes before と to introduce what the speaker notices.

1.6.n: Links looking closely with the discovery that follows.

1.7.n: Names the bird depicted in the decoration.

1.8.n: Joins 鶴 and 亀 as the two creatures noticed.

1.9.n: Names the shelled animal depicted alongside the crane.

1.10.n: Marks 鶴と亀 as the creatures that were present.

1.11.n: Polite past form of いる, normally used for living beings, here treating the depicted animals as creatures.

2.0.n: Used alone as an excited reaction, without a polite ending.

2.2.n: Names what the speaker finds cute; a particle such as は is omitted in casual speech.

2.3.n: A very casual intensifier placed before かわいい to express enthusiasm.

2.4.n: A plain-form adjective used as an excited comment without です.

0.lit: Further inside, a very large decoration of braided cord also.
0.tip: Ending with も leaves the existence verb unspoken; English naturally supplies there was also.

1.lit: The powerful presence was incredible. When looking closely, a crane and a turtle were there.
1.tip: The first と means when after a verb; the second means and between nouns.

2.tip: Casual exclamations often omit particles and polite endings, as in 亀めっちゃかわいい.
